niche_preference_profile: This user prefers interfaces that feel complete, structured, and information-rich, with clear section hierarchy, obvious primary actions, and enough visible content to avoid looking empty or unfinished. They generally like compact, well-organized layouts with strong labels and clear affordances, but they also want the screen to feel fully populated and intentional rather than sparse. For modal/alert states, they prefer centered, uncluttered presentations with restrained, neutral styling and concise copy. They show a strong preference for light, airy backgrounds in settings/onboarding screens, while also sometimes favoring darker, higher-contrast treatment in alert or management contexts.

criteria.description: Clear section grouping with strong visual separation, distinct headings, and a readable hierarchy that makes the screen feel organized.
A fuller, more populated screen with enough visible items and settings to feel complete rather than sparse or placeholder-like.
Obvious primary actions and clear row affordances, such as prominent buttons, visible controls, and easy-to-understand next steps.
A streamlined layout with fewer competing elements, less clutter, and tighter grouping that keeps attention on the main task.
Specific, descriptive labels and visible details that make items and settings easy to understand at a glance.
Centered, uncluttered modal or alert screens with simplified background context, restrained styling, and concise messaging.
